---
title: "Overview of Ecosystem Service: Extractive Energy Provision"
format:
  html:
    embed-resources: true
    standalone: true
---

Extractive energy provision covers natural gas, coal and petroleum. The account values it as the
resource rent each country earns from extraction, read from the World Bank's Changing Wealth of
Nations 2024 package at the GEP base year of 2019.

## Quantity and price

For gas and oil the quantity is CWoN's production (TJ of gas, barrels of oil) and the price is
CWoN's unit rent in current USD per unit. The rent is their product, as CWoN computes it. For coal
the module takes CWoN's published rent. CWoN builds coal rent as thermal plus metallurgical plus
brown coal, each priced from mine-level prices and costs by coal type, and the package ships those
inputs for no coal type. The price convention recorded for this service in `es_config.csv` is
`resource rent`.

## Valuation

`fuel_rent_from_production_and_unit_rent` computes gas or oil rent at the requested year. It
matches the production and unit-rent tables on `countrycode`, one to one, and multiplies. A
country missing either input has no rent, and a zero in either is a zero rent, because CWoN floors
negative unit rents at zero. Nothing is filled. A table carrying another series label, or repeating
a country code, is refused. The CWoN tables are wide, keyed on `countrycode` with World Bank codes
that match `iso3_r250_label` directly, Kosovo included as XKX.

`fuel_rent_by_country_from_cwon` reads coal's published rent at the requested year.
`compare_with_published_rent` checks the computed gas and oil rent against CWoN's published
`<fuel>_rent_cd`. In 2019 they agree in every country, 98 for gas and 99 for oil, with the same
missing countries and relative differences below 2e-16.

`extractive_energy_gep_from_cwon` joins the three components to the r250 countries, one to one,
and refuses a valued country code with no r250 row. It sums the components with `min_count=1`. A
country absent from one fuel's table stays NaN in that component and still receives a service
total from the components that do exist, so a country with only coal is a coal country rather than
a missing one. Components sum by the same commodity convention that extractive materials provision
uses.

## Inputs

From `es_parameters.csv`, all scoped to the `extractive_energy` service:

- `extractive_energy_cwon_{gas,oil}_production_path` and
  `extractive_energy_cwon_{gas,oil}_unit_rent_path`, the Stata production and unit-rent tables
  the gas and oil rent is computed from.
- `extractive_energy_cwon_gas_path`, `extractive_energy_cwon_coal_path` and
  `extractive_energy_cwon_oil_path`, the Stata published rent tables: coal's is the valuation, and
  gas's and oil's are the check.
- Each Stata table carries a `_source_url` row pointing at the World Bank reproducibility archive
  and a `_source_archive_member` row naming the file inside it, under
  `Reproducibility package/Output/Latest/`.
- `extractive_energy_gas_path`, `extractive_energy_coal_path` and `extractive_energy_oil_path`,
  the three committed per-country CSVs from the consortium drive, kept as the replication anchor.

The shared country references come from `initialize_country_paths`, which publishes the r264
correspondence and loads `p.df_countries`.

## Output

`gep_calculation` writes `gep_by_country_base_year.csv` into its own task directory. The columns
are the r250 identifiers and attributes, `year`, the three per-fuel columns
`extractive_energy_gas_gep`, `extractive_energy_coal_gep` and `extractive_energy_oil_gep`, and
their sum `extractive_energy_gep`.

## Method constants

`EXTRACTIVE_ENERGY_FUELS = ('gas', 'coal', 'oil')` names the three components and fixes the order
the summation reads them in.

`COMMITTED_DUPLICATE_VALUE_ROWS` records eight rows of the committed drive CSVs that carry another
country's full rent value. Bouvet Island and Svalbard take Norway's, Christmas Island and the
Cocos Islands take Australia's, Tokelau takes New Zealand's, Western Sahara takes Morocco's,
Palestine takes Israel's, and Kosovo takes Serbia's. In the Kosovo row the committed name column
itself reads "Serbia". The values were verified equal in every fuel where the row is non-empty.

## Taken as given

CWoN's production and unit-rent estimates for gas and oil, and its coal rent estimation, are
upstream science and are used as published.

## What is open

The eight duplicate rows are a name-join artefact that counts the source countries twice, and for
Kosovo it overrides the CWoN table's own coal value. CWoN carries no rows at all for the first
six. The module therefore computes from the CWoN tables, one country one row, rather than
adopting the committed CSVs. `gep_calculation` logs the computed total beside the committed total
so the gap stays visible on every run.

The committed CSVs also leave South Sudan empty, in oil ($3,132,215,611 in CWoN) and in coal
(zero in CWoN). Their join matches CWoN's country code against the correspondence's `adm0_a3`,
which is `SDS` for South Sudan, and the same key gives each territory its sovereign's code,
which is how the eight duplicates arise. The module reads the CWoN code directly and carries
South Sudan in both fuels.
